export.kind.camilla_dsp.body: Writes a CamillaDSP v4 configuration and a 48 kHz FIR wav file per channel. With MIMO included, the support paths go into the configuration too.
export.kind.before_after_mdat.body: Writes one mdat file for REW. Each channel gets the measurement before correction and the computed response after it, plus the MIMO-applied response when MIMO is included. Subs are added as measured.
export.kind.staged_mdat.body: Writes one mdat file with computed responses per stage for each channel: main and sub before correction, the XO target, the correction after summing and MIMO applied. Use it to compare in REW what each stage changed.
help.title: Help · {step}
help.step.label: Step {n} of {total}
help.system.intro.body.1: You can walk from System to Export once without a microphone or REW.
help.system.intro.body.2: The tutorial opens a separate project of the demo room (7.1.4 · 3 subs). Your project stays as it is, and you return to it when the tutorial ends.
help.system.intro.body.3: During the tutorial the accent turns magenta and the rail shows 'Tutorial'. Measuring is simulated, so nothing plays, and the project cannot be saved or exported.
help.system.intro.body.4: You do not need REW Pro. Measure with this app's own measurement, or import mdat files measured in REW under Measure & import. Automatic measuring through REW needs REW Pro in API mode.
help.system.intro.route.1: System: the demo room setup and a one-position arrangement are already filled in.
help.system.intro.route.2: Connect & check: the measuring method is the simulation. Press 'Check every channel's level'.
help.system.intro.route.3: Measure & import: fill position 1 with 'Demo data'.
help.system.intro.route.4: Correction: press 'Compute correction', then go through the SPL, GD, XO and BA tabs.
help.system.intro.route.5: Export: the tutorial saves nothing. In a real project this writes the CamillaDSP configuration and REW mdat files.
help.system.intro.route.6: End: 'End tutorial' in the tutorial list returns to your project.
help.system.intro.outro.1: Press F1 on any step to open its help. The screen stays usable while help is open.
help.system.steps.goal: Record which speaker is wired to which output, and decide how many positions to measure. The measuring order and the export channels follow this table.
help.system.steps.1.do: Pick the preset that matches the room under Setup.
help.system.steps.1.see: The output table fills with one row per speaker. 7.1.4 has 12 rows; the demo room has two more subs, so 14.
help.system.steps.2.see: Each sub adds or removes a row. You can have 0–8 subs.
help.system.steps.3.do: If a speaker is missing, press 'Add speaker'.
help.system.steps.3.see: A new row appears below the table. Remove rows you do not need with the remove button at the end of the row.
help.system.steps.4.do: Match each row's measurement output to the real wiring.
help.system.steps.4.see: A duplicate number, or one beyond the device's outputs, is marked in its cell and listed below the table.
help.system.steps.5.see: Set polarity to inverted only for speakers wired in reverse. Size can stay as the preset set it: small applies the XO, large plays full range.
help.system.steps.6.do: Pick your DSP device under Export DSP.
help.system.steps.6.see: The filter resources change to that device's values. The FIR budget feeds the correction's FIR budget warning and the MIMO FIR support budget. Editing a value makes the profile custom.
help.system.steps.7.do: Under Measurement arrangement, pick the one that fits where you listen.
help.system.steps.7.see: One spot (the listening position only) is for a quick check. For a single chair pick One chair (9 positions); for a sofa pick Two-seat sofa (13) or Family, two rows (17).
help.system.steps.8.see: Position 1 is the listening position and the reference for level and delay alignment. Half-filled markers are positions with the microphone 20 cm higher or lower.
help.system.steps.9.do: Check the timing reference and the reference speaker.
help.system.steps.9.see: Keep the default, 'Acoustic: reference speaker'. The reference speaker cannot be a sub.
help.system.steps.10.see: It shows the time per position and the total. Moving the microphone is not included.
help.system.steps.11.do: Press 'Go to Connect & check' in the header.
help.system.steps.11.see: This opens Connect & check. Press a step in the rail to come back here.
help.system.checks.1: The measurement output is the output number of the audio device the sweep plays from. Patch the DSP inputs by the same numbers.
help.system.checks.2: Changing the preset, the sub count or the arrangement clears existing measurements. With measurements present a confirmation opens first, and the notification after the change can undo it.
help.system.checks.3: Keep positions at least 30 cm apart and the whole spread at least 1 m across.
help.system.checks.4: Spread the height too, ear height ±20 cm.
help.system.checks.5: Measure at least 5 positions for real use. MIMO needs 3 positions or more.
help.system.checks.6: With the timing reference set to 'None', distance, delay and BA cannot be computed.
help.system.trouble.1.symptom: 'Go to Connect & check' cannot be pressed.
help.system.trouble.1.fix: The reason is under the header. Usually two rows share an output or a speaker has none. Duplicate numbers can be fixed with 'Renumber outputs'.
help.system.trouble.2.symptom: The measurement output device shows no channel count.
help.system.trouble.2.fix: The measurement output device is chosen under Connect & check. Its channel count appears once it is chosen.
help.system.trouble.3.symptom: The time estimate is too long.
help.system.trouble.3.fix: Pick an arrangement with fewer positions, or shorten the sweep under Connect & check. Shorter sweeps pick up more noise.
help.system.trouble.4.symptom: The speaker you want is not in the reference list.
help.system.trouble.4.fix: The list follows the setup table. A sub cannot be the reference.
help.system.trouble.5.symptom: Timing looks wrong with the loopback reference.
help.system.trouble.5.fix: Connect a spare output to a spare input with a cable. Choose the loopback input channel under Connect & check; when measuring with REW, set the reference input in REW as well.
help.system.real.1: The audio interface and the DSP must be wired by the table's output numbers. A wrong number plays a different speaker.
help.system.real.2: 'Patch sheet CSV' saves the table for patching the DSP inputs.
help.system.real.3: Enter your device's FIR taps and FIR budget under Export DSP, and the correction warns about results that will not fit that device.
help.system.real.4: In practice you move the microphone for every position. A start delay gives you time to step away after pressing measure.
help.system.real.5: With the acoustic reference, the reference speaker plays a short reference signal before every sweep. Hearing an extra sound is expected.
help.system.real.6: Adding a few points 20–30 cm outside the sofa prevents overcorrection.
help.connect.steps.goal: Choose how to measure, check the devices and the microphone, then set the microphone level for every channel. When you only import mdat files measured in REW, this step is skipped.
help.connect.steps.1.see: Own measurement plays and records the sweep through your audio devices. REW drives REW Pro in API mode. The simulation uses synthesised responses and plays nothing. 'Import mdat files only' skips this step.
help.connect.steps.2.do: With REW, press 'Launch REW in API mode'.
help.connect.steps.2.see: If REW is not running it starts (10–20 s). Continue when the state reads 'API connected · 127.0.0.1:4735'. If REW is already running, press 'Check again'.
help.connect.steps.3.see: With Pro confirmed, this app runs the sweeps through REW. Without Pro, measure in REW yourself and import the mdat files.
help.connect.steps.4.do: Set the input device and channel to the measurement microphone.
help.connect.steps.4.see: Own measurement lists the system's devices; REW lists REW's. Continue when the microphone appears.
help.connect.steps.5.do: Check the output device, the microphone calibration and the sweep length.
help.connect.steps.5.see: The output device is the measurement output device System refers to. Keep the sweep length at the default 256k (about 5.5 s).
help.connect.steps.6.do: Place the microphone at ear height at the listening position and start with the master output low.
help.connect.steps.6.see: Start quiet and raise the level step by step.
help.connect.steps.7.do: Press play on the first channel.
help.connect.steps.7.see: It plays for 2.5 s: a 50 Hz sine on subs, pink noise elsewhere. The meter should land in the target band (−30…−15 dBFS).
help.connect.steps.8.do: If the meter is too low or too high, move the master output and play again.
help.connect.steps.8.see: The current level (dBFS) shows at the end of the row.
help.connect.steps.9.do: Press 'Check every channel's level' in the header.
help.connect.steps.9.see: The channels play in turn and their values fill in. When every channel has a level, Connect & check is marked done in the rail.
help.connect.checks.1: REW must run with the -api option. A plainly started REW does not connect.
help.connect.checks.2: Make sure the input channel is the one the microphone is plugged into. Otherwise the level meter does not move.
help.connect.checks.3: Check that every channel lands in the target band. If one channel is far lower, check its wiring and amplifier first.
help.connect.checks.4: REW output above −6 dBFS must be unlocked in REW. Start low to protect the speakers.
help.connect.checks.5: Change the microphone gain on the audio device or in REW, not in this app.
help.connect.checks.6: 'Skip with default levels' fills every channel with a value inside the target band. Use it only to see the flow.
help.connect.trouble.1.fix: If REW runs without -api, close it and press 'Launch REW in API mode' again. Once the REW window is up, press 'Check again'.
help.connect.trouble.2.symptom: The input device list is empty.
help.connect.trouble.2.fix: With REW, press 'Check again' after REW connects to read the list again. With own measurement, the list fills again when the device is plugged in.
help.connect.trouble.3.fix: REW cannot measure automatically. Switch to own measurement, or import mdat files measured in REW under Measure & import.
help.connect.trouble.4.fix: REW did not report that value. Check it in REW itself.
help.connect.trouble.5.symptom: The level meter does not move at all.
help.connect.trouble.5.fix: Check that the input device and channel match the microphone.
help.connect.trouble.6.fix: Compare its measurement output under System with the real wiring.
help.connect.trouble.7.symptom: The meter goes above the target band.
help.connect.trouble.7.fix: Lower the master output. Too high a level can clip the sweep.
help.connect.trouble.8.symptom: The device refuses the chosen sharing mode.
help.connect.trouble.8.fix: On Windows a device can refuse a fixed exclusive or shared mode. Set the sharing mode to automatic.
help.connect.real.1: To measure with REW, start it first as roomeqwizard.exe -api.
help.connect.real.2: This app runs sweeps through REW only with a REW Pro licence. Without one, use own measurement, or measure in REW and import the mdat files.
help.connect.real.3: With REW, the input device, channel and microphone calibration are read from REW's settings. If REW uses a different calibration per input, this screen cannot tell.
help.connect.real.4: The level check plays pink noise, and a 50 Hz sine on subs. Keep the room quiet so the values stay steady.
help.connect.real.5: When the level check ends, the recommended sweep level is stored in the measurement settings and the sweeps in Measure & import play at that level.
help.connect.real.6: The simulation plays nothing and uses responses synthesised for the demo room. Use it to learn the flow.
help.measure.steps.goal: Place the microphone where the map shows and sweep every channel at each position. You can also import mdat files measured in REW.
help.measure.steps.1.do: Look at 'Position k / N' and the map.
help.measure.steps.1.see: The position to measure next is shown in the accent colour on the map. You can also pick it in the position list.
help.measure.steps.2.do: Put the microphone there and press 'Measure this position' in the header.
help.measure.steps.2.see: Each channel sweeps in turn. If the project has never been saved, a window to choose where to save it opens first.
help.measure.steps.3.see: The job tray shows progress, elapsed and remaining time. To stop, press 'Cancel measurement' or Cancel in the tray.
help.measure.steps.4.do: Look at the graph and the position list.
help.measure.steps.4.see: The graph draws the channel curves and the position turns done in the list.
help.measure.steps.5.do: If more positions remain, move the microphone and press 'Measure this position' again.
help.measure.steps.5.see: After each position, the next one is selected.
help.measure.steps.6.do: Check that every position is done.
help.measure.steps.6.see: 'All measured' appears and Measure & import is marked done in the rail.
help.measure.steps.7.do: If you measured in REW, press 'Import mdat'.
help.measure.steps.7.see: After you pick a file, a window opens to assign a channel and position to each measurement. Check the values filled in from the names and press 'Import'. The 'mdat import' tab has the details.
help.measure.checks.1: Measuring needs a saved project. A new project that was never saved asks for a location before measuring.
help.measure.checks.2: To redo a suspicious position, select it in the list and measure again; only that record changes.
help.measure.checks.3: If a warning says the signal-to-noise ratio is below 20 dB, raise the level or use a longer sweep.
help.measure.checks.4: The position cannot change while measuring.
help.measure.checks.5: With the acoustic timing reference, repeats are fixed at 1.
help.measure.checks.6: You can save one mdat file per position and import each. Add _P2 to the names of position 2's measurements. Example: L_P2
help.measure.trouble.1.fix: Look for a signal-to-noise warning. Raise the level or lengthen the sweep under Connect & check.
help.measure.trouble.2.symptom: One channel's curve is far lower.
help.measure.trouble.2.fix: Check its output number under System and the wiring. Measure the position again after fixing it.
help.measure.trouble.3.symptom: The last position was measured wrong.
help.measure.trouble.3.fix: 'Redo last position' clears it and measures it again. The notification after clearing can undo it.
help.measure.trouble.4.fix: Stop it with 'Cancel measurement' and check under Connect & check that the measuring path is connected.
help.measure.real.1: A real run takes the channel count × the sweep length. 7.1.4 at 256k takes about 1 min 30 s per position.
help.measure.real.2: Keep the room quiet and leave the microphone alone during the sweeps.
help.measure.real.3: Without REW Pro, measure in REW and bring the files in with 'Import mdat'. The correction is the same as for measurements made here.
help.measure.real.4: The demo data is a real measurement of the demo room at its listening position only. For real use, measure 5 positions or more.
help.measure.mdat.start.2: Measure each channel in REW, save the measurements as an .mdat file, then press 'Import mdat' under Measure & import.
help.measure.mdat.s1.head: Naming measurements in REW
help.measure.mdat.s1.1: A measurement's name is the channel name plus the position number.
help.measure.mdat.s1.2: Position 1 uses the channel name only. Example: L, SW1
help.measure.mdat.s1.3: From position 2, add _P2, _P3 to the name. Example: L_P2
help.measure.mdat.s2.head: The window that opens after picking a file
help.measure.mdat.s2.1: Each row shows a measurement name from REW.
help.measure.mdat.s2.2: The channel and position recognised from the name are filled in.
help.measure.mdat.s2.3: Each row says whether the measurement is unreadable, low frequencies only (looks like a sub) or full range.
help.measure.mdat.s2.4: Names that are not recognised are set to 'Skip'. Pick a channel to use them.
help.measure.mdat.s2.5: If everything is right, press 'Import'. A row with a problem turns Import off.
help.measure.mdat.s3.head: One file per position works too
help.measure.mdat.s3.1: Pressing 'Import mdat' twice fills positions 1 and 2 in turn.
help.measure.mdat.s3.2: 'Manage files' imports a whole file into a chosen position, or clears just that position.
help.measure.mdat.s3.3: Only the file's positions and channels are replaced; other measurements stay.
help.measure.mdat.s4.head: Channel names
help.measure.mdat.s4.1: A name without a number, such as SUB, SW or LFE, means SW1.
help.measure.mdat.s4.2: With several subs, add the number as in SW2. 'SW 2' with a space reads as position 2.
help.measure.mdat.s5.head: Names that are not recognised
help.measure.mdat.s5.2: DBA L: DBA comes before L.
help.measure.mdat.s5.4: Pick the channel for such measurements in the window.
help.measure.mdat.s6.head: Keep in mind
help.measure.mdat.s6.1: Set the timing reference to Acoustic when measuring in REW, so the time differences between channels are kept.
help.measure.mdat.s6.2: The number of positions is set under System's measurement arrangement. Higher position numbers are skipped.
help.calibrate.steps.goal: Choose a correction mode, press 'Compute correction', then go through the SPL, GD, XO and BA tabs and change only what needs it. Changing a setting marks the result 'Recompute needed'; the result changes only when you compute again.
help.calibrate.steps.1.do: Choose the correction mode and press 'Compute correction' in the header.
help.calibrate.steps.1.see: The mode is how much delay the correction filters may add. Minimum delay corrects magnitude only; Low latency and Standard use more delay to correct the low-frequency phase too. The first run recommends the XO first; the job tray shows progress and the time left.
help.calibrate.steps.2.do: Look at the verdict card and the per-channel scorecard.
help.calibrate.steps.2.see: The share of 20–200 Hz within ±1 dB of the target should grow, and the 20–100 Hz GD spread should shrink. Select a channel in the scorecard to show it in the graph.
help.calibrate.steps.3.do: On the SPL tab, compare the before and after curves with the dashed target.
help.calibrate.steps.3.see: The shaded area outside is where RC does not act. Inside it, an after curve that follows the target evenly is a good correction; narrow deep dips are deliberately not filled. Drag points to edit the target; right-click empty space for the flat, Harman and cinema presets.
help.calibrate.steps.4.see: GD is how late sound arrives at each frequency. Lower low-frequency peaks and a flatter curve are better.
help.calibrate.steps.5.do: Set the band to correct and the boost limit under Correction range.
help.calibrate.steps.5.see: The automatic upper limit comes from the room volume or dimensions. The boost limit caps every boost of RC, XO PEQ and the sub bus PEQ.
help.calibrate.steps.6.do: On the XO tab, pick a channel and look at the XO and XO PEQ.
help.calibrate.steps.6.see: It draws the channel's main, sub and their sum. A good XO has a sum that follows the target without dips or bumps around the XO. Drag the vertical line to change the XO; the automatic XO PEQ upper limit is XO × 4.
help.calibrate.steps.7.do: With two subs or more, look at the graph and value table on the BA tab.
help.calibrate.steps.7.see: Each colour is one sub; dashed is before alignment, solid after, and the thick line is the sub sum. A flat sum without dips and small sub-sum flatness and seat spread figures are better. The table lists each sub's gain, delay, polarity and all-pass for the DSP.
help.calibrate.steps.8.do: Under Sub alignment (BA), set the infra sub and each sub's mode.
help.calibrate.steps.8.see: Choosing an infra sub puts a LP on it and the matching HP on the other subs. Automatic lets the engine find the values, Fixed uses the values as entered, and a group keeps the relative values of its subs. After a change, 'Compute subs only' recomputes just the BA tab. Odd settings show a warning.
help.calibrate.steps.9.do: With 3 positions or more you can turn on MIMO and press 'Compute MIMO'.
help.calibrate.steps.9.see: Support filters are IIR by default (PEQ 9 + all-pass 3) and take a few minutes. FIR supports use an 8,000-tap FIR per support: about a minute and stronger low-frequency damping, but many FIR taps, which suits PC DSPs such as CamillaDSP. When it ends, the SPL tab draws the MIMO-applied curve.
help.calibrate.checks.1: Changing a setting such as the mode, range, target, XO or sub values marks the result 'Recompute needed'. Nothing recomputes on its own.
help.calibrate.checks.2: 'Take result values' copies the last result's sub gain, delay, polarity and all-pass into the fields without computing. A 'Compute subs only' result shows on the BA tab only; compute the correction again to export it.
help.calibrate.checks.3: Grouped subs keep the gain, delay, polarity and all-pass you entered relative to each other; the engine sets only the group's common gain, delay and polarity.
help.calibrate.checks.4: The XO recommendation computes the full correction for each candidate (60, 80, 100, 120 Hz), takes the best per group and computes again. It takes a few minutes.
help.calibrate.checks.5: MIMO is a separate heavy computation that shortens low-frequency decay. Computing the correction again keeps the MIMO result but marks it 'Recompute needed'.
help.calibrate.checks.6: The ultra latency mode (30–200 ms) can be chosen only with 'Show expert items' on in Settings.
help.calibrate.trouble.1.fix: Measure, or import mdat files, under Measure & import.
help.calibrate.trouble.2.fix: It needs 3 measured positions or more, MIMO turned on, and a correction result first.
help.calibrate.trouble.3.fix: Cancel in the job tray stops it. Standard mode, the XO recommendation and MIMO (IIR) take long. MIMO is much faster with FIR supports.
help.calibrate.trouble.4.fix: 'Almost no passband' means the sub's LP is below twice its HP, so it plays almost nothing; check the fixed filters for a LP on a sub that is not the infra sub. 'Gain too high' means a sub gain above +12 dB, possibly filling a blocked band with gain. Fix the filters and check again with 'Compute subs only'.
help.calibrate.real.1: More positions and channels take longer to compute. The job tray shows the time left.
help.calibrate.real.2: BA searches each sub's polarity and delay within ±12 ms of its arrival and weighs the summing efficiency, how well the subs add up, along with flatness. Less cancellation gives more maximum bass level from the same amplifiers.
help.calibrate.real.3: Graphs and figures are computed. Measure again after loading the DSP to confirm.
help.export.steps.goal: Export the correction as a CamillaDSP configuration and as a REW mdat file that compares before and after.
help.export.steps.1.do: See what will be exported under 'Correction to export'.
help.export.steps.1.see: It shows the correction mode, total delay, channels, the RC range and whether MIMO is included.
help.export.steps.2.do: Press 'Export CamillaDSP configuration' in the header.
help.export.steps.2.see: The export folder's camilladsp folder receives the configuration (secs_<mode>.yml in configs) and 48 kHz FIR wav files (in coeffs). It has the CamillaDSP folder layout, so it can be copied as it is. The configuration holds the input PEQ and FIR, the bass management XO, the sub bus gain, delay, polarity and PEQ, and the LFE (+10 dB, 120 Hz) to every sub; with MIMO included, the support paths too.
help.export.steps.3.see: One file, 'SECS 보정 전후 <mode>.mdat', is saved; open it with File > Open in REW. Each channel has <number>_<channel>_1 before, _2 after and _3 + MIMO. _1 is the listening position measurement as is, _2 is the computed channel correction with the sub sum, and _3 appears only with MIMO included. Subs follow at the end, as measured.
help.export.steps.4.do: Open the saved files with 'Open folder'.
help.export.steps.4.see: By default this is the '<date> <project name>' folder under SECS_export next to the project. REW mdat goes into a SECS_mdat_RC_BA(_MIMO)_<mode>_<time> folder inside it, and the CamillaDSP configuration into camilladsp.
help.export.steps.5.do: If needed, save 'Staged mdat' under Advanced.
help.export.steps.5.see: Each channel gets computed responses for the main and sub before correction, the XO target, the correction after summing and MIMO applied (when included). Use it to compare in REW what each stage changed.
help.export.steps.6.do: See the 'CamillaDSP' tab for loading it into CamillaDSP.
help.export.steps.6.see: The devices are test files (in.raw, out.raw); change them to the loopback and the interface in the GUI. For routing, change only the numbers in route_in and route_out on the Mixers tab.
help.export.checks.1: Nothing can be exported without a result or while it needs recomputing. Compute it under Correction.
help.export.checks.2: MIMO is included only when it is turned on, computed, and 3 positions or more are measured. Then the folder name gets _MIMO and the mdat gets a '+ MIMO' measurement.
help.export.checks.3: The mdat levels use the REW SPL offset from the measurement.
help.export.trouble.1.symptom: The export buttons cannot be pressed.
help.export.trouble.1.fix: Check that a result exists, that nothing is computing and that it does not need recomputing. The reason is under the header.
help.export.trouble.2.symptom: The export files could not be written.
help.export.trouble.2.fix: Check the export folder's location and write permission, or pick another folder with 'Change…' and export again.
help.export.trouble.3.symptom: The mdat levels look wrong in REW.
help.export.trouble.3.fix: Check that the measurement in REW kept its SPL offset. Imported mdat files keep their original offset.
help.export.real.1: Load the exported configuration into CamillaDSP. Turn the amplifiers off before switching.
help.export.real.2: After applying it, measure again at the listening position and compare with the mdat's after curves.
help.export.real.3: Every correction mode delays the sound. The total delay is under 'Correction to export' and at the top of the configuration file. For video, advance the player's audio sync by that much.
help.export.camilla.start.1: This is how to listen to the SECS 2R correction through CamillaDSP, from a PC with nothing installed to sound.
help.export.camilla.start.2: The order is the same on Windows and macOS. It follows CamillaDSP 4.1; screen names may differ slightly between versions.
help.export.camilla.s1.head: Four things to get
help.export.camilla.s1.1: CamillaDSP: release 4.1.3 from github.com/HEnquist/camilladsp. Just unpack it.
help.export.camilla.s1.3: Loopback: VB-CABLE (vb-audio.com) on Windows, BlackHole on macOS.
help.export.camilla.s1.4: Audio interface: the one you use now.
help.export.camilla.s2.head: The signal path
help.export.camilla.s2.1: Loopback: CamillaDSP takes the sound from here (capture device).
help.export.camilla.s2.3: Interface: CamillaDSP plays out here (playback device).
help.export.camilla.s2.4: Send the player's sound to the loopback: on Windows make CABLE Input the default playback device, on macOS set the sound output to BlackHole.
help.export.camilla.s2.5: VB-CABLE on Windows is reliable for stereo. For 12 channels such as 7.1.4, BlackHole 16ch on macOS is easier.
help.export.camilla.s3.head: Make the CamillaDSP folder first
help.export.camilla.s3.1: bin and gui: unpack the downloads here.
help.export.camilla.s3.2: configs and coeffs: create these empty folders beforehand. Without them the GUI closes right after starting.
help.export.camilla.s3.3: If your user name has non-Latin characters, create it at a Latin path such as C:\camilladsp and fix the paths in the GUI's settings file: gui\camillagui_backend\_internal\config\camillagui.yml
help.export.camilla.s4.head: Copy the exported files
help.export.camilla.s4.1: The exported camilladsp folder has the CamillaDSP folder layout. Copy the files of both folders as they are.
help.export.camilla.s4.2: The yml in configs → CamillaDSP's configs
help.export.camilla.s4.3: The wav files in coeffs → CamillaDSP's coeffs. The configuration refers to ../coeffs/, so they open as they are.
help.export.camilla.s4.4: in.raw is for SECS 2R's own checks; do not copy it.
help.export.camilla.s5.head: Starting: two windows and a browser
help.export.camilla.s5.1: Run the commands in the camilladsp folder. On Windows, type cmd into that folder's address bar.
help.export.camilla.s5.2: Keep the CamillaDSP engine window open. Closing it stops the sound.
help.export.camilla.s5.3: -g-20 starts at −20 dB volume. Turn the amplifiers down at first as well.
help.export.camilla.s5.4: On macOS, allow 'Terminal would like to access the microphone'. If denied, there is silence without an error.
help.export.camilla.s6.head: Uploading in the GUI: Files tab
help.export.camilla.s6.1: If you copied the files, just press the star next to the configuration under Configs.
help.export.camilla.s6.2: Upload all wav files from coeffs first, with Upload files under Filters.
help.export.camilla.s6.3: Then upload the yml with Upload files under Configs.
help.export.camilla.s6.4: Valid should show a green check; otherwise hover over it for the reason.
help.export.camilla.s6.5: The star makes it the active configuration and loads it into the GUI.
help.export.camilla.s6.6: Without the wav files it still shows Valid and fails when applied, so upload the wav files first.
help.export.camilla.s6.7: Files with the same name are overwritten without a question.
help.export.camilla.s7.head: Devices tab
help.export.camilla.s7.2: Capture device is the loopback; set channels to route_in's in.
help.export.camilla.s7.3: Playback device is the interface; set channels to route_out's out.
help.export.camilla.s7.4: The two devices have different clocks, so turn on Rate adjust. On Windows set the resampler to AsyncSinc.
help.export.camilla.s7.5: Pick device names with the magnifier. The list appears only while the CamillaDSP window runs.
help.export.camilla.s7.6: On macOS set type to CoreAudio and capture to BlackHole 16ch, and leave the resampler empty.
help.export.camilla.s7.7: Leave format empty. F32_LE gives an error.
help.export.camilla.s7.8: On Windows set Sound control panel › device Properties › Advanced › Default format to 48000 Hz for both devices.
help.export.camilla.s7.9: Start chunksize at 1024; use 2048 if the sound drops out, 512 to lower latency.
help.export.camilla.s8.head: The channel order at the top of the configuration
help.export.camilla.s8.1: The comment at the top of the configuration lists the input order (what CamillaDSP receives) and the output order (what it plays out).
help.export.camilla.s8.2: Numbers start at 0: interface output 1 is 0.
help.export.camilla.s8.3: Saving from the GUI removes this comment. The same order is in the Title tab's description.
help.export.camilla.s9.head: If the player's order differs: route_in on the Mixers tab
help.export.camilla.s9.1: Most players send LFE fourth. SECS 2R's inputs have LFE last.
help.export.camilla.s9.2: Columns are the channels the player sends, numbered from 0. Move only the cells of the Ls, Rs and LFE rows.
help.export.camilla.s9.3: Pressing a cell opens a small window. Delete the connection and press + on the new cell.
help.export.camilla.s9.4: The Windows 7.1 order is FL FR FC LFE BL BR SL SR: back before side.
help.export.camilla.s10.head: If the wiring differs: route_out
help.export.camilla.s10.1: Example: the sub on interface output 4, the surrounds on 5 and 6.
help.export.camilla.s10.2: out is the interface's output count. Change the playback channels under Devices to match.
help.export.camilla.s10.3: Move only the cells of the output 4, 5 and 6 rows. CamillaDSP's numbers are one lower.
help.export.camilla.s11.head: Apply and check
help.export.camilla.s11.1: Apply to DSP sends the GUI's configuration to CamillaDSP.
help.export.camilla.s11.2: State RUNNING means it is running. The input and output meters move when the player plays.
help.export.camilla.s11.3: Play one channel at a time and check that the right speaker sounds, with a channel test file or REW's signal generator.
help.export.camilla.s11.4: If Clipped samples grows, lower the player's volume or the GUI's Volume.
help.export.camilla.s11.5: When it works, press Save to file. From then on, starting the CamillaDSP window plays with the last configuration.
help.export.camilla.s12.head: Latency: video sync
help.export.camilla.s12.1: Every correction mode delays the sound. The latency is at the top of the configuration file and on the Title tab.
help.export.camilla.s12.2: For video, advance the player's audio sync by that much: −200 ms for 200 ms ultra latency.
help.export.camilla.s13.head: Common problems
help.export.camilla.s13.1: The GUI closes at once: create the configs and coeffs folders inside camilladsp.
help.export.camilla.s13.2: State Offline: the CamillaDSP window is closed or was started without -p1234.
help.export.camilla.s13.3: State STALLED: the player plays to a device other than the loopback.
help.export.camilla.s13.4: RUNNING but silent: on macOS check the microphone permission; on Windows the default playback device and 48000 Hz.
help.export.camilla.s13.5: wrong number of channels: make the device channels equal to route_in's in and route_out's out.
help.export.camilla.s13.6: unknown variant F32_LE: empty the device's format.
help.export.camilla.s13.7: Dropouts every few minutes: turn on Rate adjust; on Windows also use the AsyncSinc resampler, and raise chunksize if it continues.
help.export.camilla.s13.8: Unable to find coefficient file: check that the wav files are in coeffs.

tutorial.end.body: You went from System to Export with the demo room. For real use, choose a measuring method and measure several positions: 9 or more for one chair.
tutorial.glossary.rew: Room EQ Wizard, a measurement program. This app can also run its sweeps through REW.
tutorial.glossary.api: The connection through which this app drives REW. It needs REW Pro, and REW must start with the -api option.
tutorial.glossary.calibration: A file (.cal) that corrects the measurement microphone's frequency response.
tutorial.glossary.sweep: A measurement signal that glides from low to high frequencies (a log sine).
tutorial.glossary.polarity: Whether a speaker pushes or pulls (+/−). When two speakers play the same band with opposite polarity, the bass cancels.
tutorial.glossary.dsp: The processor that runs the correction filters, such as CamillaDSP, Tesira or miniDSP.
tutorial.glossary.fir: A filter that corrects magnitude and phase together. More taps give finer low-frequency resolution.
tutorial.glossary.iir: Short filters such as parametric EQ (PEQ) bands, counted in bands.
tutorial.glossary.dbfs: Level relative to digital full scale, 0 dBFS. −20 dBFS is 20 dB below full scale.
tutorial.glossary.timing: A reference signal played with the sweep so that every channel's arrival time is measured on the same clock.
tutorial.glossary.mimo: Multi-Input Multi-Output: a correction that uses several speakers to shorten the ringing and decay of low-frequency room modes.
tutorial.glossary.mdat: REW's file for a set of measurements.
tutorial.glossary.rc: Room Correction: it tames the peaks and dips the room puts into the frequency response.
tutorial.glossary.spl: The frequency response graph. Correction draws it with the target level at 0 dB.
tutorial.glossary.target: The curve the correction aims for.
tutorial.glossary.gd: Group delay: the arrival delay at each frequency. It grows where room modes ring long.
tutorial.glossary.xo: Crossover: the frequency where mains and subs split the band.
tutorial.glossary.peq: A parametric EQ band set by frequency, gain and Q.
tutorial.glossary.boost: The most the correction may raise the level, which protects headroom and drivers.
tutorial.glossary.lp_hp: A low-pass cuts the highs; a high-pass cuts the lows.
tutorial.glossary.gain: The value (dB) that raises or lowers the level.
tutorial.glossary.delay: The value (ms) that holds a signal back on purpose, aligning each sub's arrival.
tutorial.glossary.allpass: A filter that leaves magnitude alone and turns only the phase around one frequency.
tutorial.glossary.dba: Double Bass Array: front-wall and rear-wall subs, the rear ones delayed with opposite polarity, cancelling bass reflections.
tutorial.sample.rail.title: Step rail
tutorial.sample.rail: The rail: the five steps and the state of each. A blocked step shows a lock and a short reason; open it to see what it needs.
tutorial.sample.rail.why: The steps build on each other. A step's main action turns on once the steps before it are done.
tutorial.sample.status.title: Project status
tutorial.sample.status: Project status: setup, measured positions, correction, measuring path and file in one place.
tutorial.sample.help.title: Open help
tutorial.sample.help.why: Each step has a walkthrough, checks and troubleshooting. Help does not block the screen, so you can follow it while working.
tutorial.sample.tray.title: Job tray
tutorial.sample.tray: The job tray: progress, cancel and history of long jobs such as measuring, computing the correction or MIMO, and exporting.
tutorial.sample.tray.why: Long jobs never block the screen, and Cancel in the tray really stops them.
tutorial.sample.compute.title: Compute the correction
tutorial.sample.compute.why: Measuring alone changes nothing; computing produces the filters for the DSP.
tutorial.sample.compute.busy: Computing. Progress shows in the job tray; the tutorial moves on when it ends.

project.new.fixed: The demo room's setup and sub count are fixed.

project.unsaved.body_untitled: This project has never been saved.
project.unsaved.loss: Without saving, changes since the last save are lost.
project.unsaved.loss_tutorial: Ending the tutorial reopens this project from its file; unsaved changes are not kept.

project.unsaved.where: Saving first opens a window to choose the location.
project.tutorial.title: Start the tutorial
project.tutorial.lead: Walk from System to Export without a microphone or REW.
project.tutorial.point.project: A separate project of the demo room (7.1.4 · 3 subs) opens.
project.tutorial.point.measure: Measuring is simulated, so nothing plays. The demo data is a real measurement of the demo room's listening position.
project.tutorial.point.blocked: The project cannot be saved or exported during the tutorial.
project.tutorial.point.return: The tutorial list can hide it for now, restart it or end it. Ending it returns to the current project.
project.tutorial.dirty: There are unsaved changes, so a window to choose whether to save opens first.
